claim_verdicts.evidence: Round 2: deploy.sh @ stage-2 lines 10-16: `kubectl apply -f deploy/k8s/namespace.yaml -o name` (line 11), then `scripts/dev-secrets.sh >/dev/null`, `scripts/k8s/secrets.sh >/dev/null`, `kubectl get secrets -n donhang -o name`. Section 2 now says "Right after the namespace, it runs `secrets.sh`", consistent with the code.

secrets.sh @ stage-2 lines 13-15 `set -a; . ./.env; set +a`; lines 22-27 `kubectl create secret generic "$name" -n donhang "$@" --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f - -o name`; lines 29-31 `secret db`, `secret api`, `secret keycloak`.

secrets.sh @ stage-2 line 29 `secret db --from-literal=POSTGRES_PASSWORD="$POSTGRES_PASSWORD"`, line 30 `secret api --from-literal=ConnectionStrings__Default="Host=db;Database=donhang;Username=donhang;Password=$POSTGRES_PASSWORD"`.

secret.md: "The values for all keys in the `data` field have to be base64-encoded strings." managing-secret-using-kubectl.md shows `kubectl get secret db-user-pass -o jsonpath='{.data.password}' | base64 --decode` recovering the value with no key.

Resource Tracking (3.1): "Argo CD uses the `argocd.argoproj.io/tracking-id` annotation to track application resources"; a resource the tracking annotation does not reference "will neither affect the application's sync status nor be marked for pruning." Automated sync: self-heal syncs "when the live cluster's state deviates from the state defined in Git".

git-filter-branch: removing "a file (containing confidential information ...) from all commits" requires rewriting; "The rewritten history will have different object names for all the objects and will not converge with the original branch." Others may "merge old and new history and end up with multiple copies of each commit, some of which have unwanted or sensitive files".

Argo CD 3.1 Secret Management: destination-cluster approach - "secrets are populated on the destination cluster, and Argo CD does not need to directly manage them." Manifest-generation approach - "Argo CD's manifest generation step is used to inject secrets."

Round 2: ledger and section 6 now match the docs: "Argo CD needs access to the secrets, which increases the risk of leaking them." "Argo CD stores generated manifests in plaintext in its Redis cache ... the secrets are available to anyone who has access to the Redis instance or to the repo-server." Lesson: "anyone with access to Argo CD's internal components can read every one of them"; q5 d mirrors it.

dev-secrets.sh @ stage-2: `if ! grep -q '^KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD=' .env 2>/dev/null; then echo "KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD=$(openssl rand -hex 16)" >> .env`; comment: "random, so every learner's lab has its own". POSTGRES_PASSWORD is the fixed `donhang-dev-password`.

Round 2: deploy.sh @ stage-2 lines 21-28 build ConfigMaps db-init and keycloak-realm with `kubectl create configmap ... --from-file=... --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -`. Stage-3 config repo holds envs/staging/db-init.yaml and keycloak-realm.yaml. Ledger and section 5 now state exactly this.

stage-3 envs/staging/api.yaml:3-5 "the connection string from the Secret api, which the Sealed Secrets controller makes from sealed-api.yaml (scripts/devops/seal-secrets.sh adds that file)." seal-secrets.sh:23 writes "$config_repo/envs/staging/sealed-$name.yaml". envs/production has no sealed-*.yaml.

Conditional design judgement taken from outline item 5; the lesson states the conditions (lab needs only cluster and repo; shared secrets / values changed without a commit). Not a documented behaviour.
Tautological: a clone contains every committed file; private repository access controls who can clone, not what a clone holds. No version-dependent behaviour.

secret.md: "By default, Secrets are required. None of a Pod's containers will start until all non-optional Secrets are available." envs/staging db.yaml:15 sync-wave "0", api.yaml:15 sync-wave "2". Capture dr-drill-without-sealing-key.txt:24-27: "db's Pod, waiting / CreateContainerConfigError / the api (wave 2): never applied, the sync stops at wave 0 / deployments.apps \"api\" not found".

stage-2 deploy/k8s/api.yaml: `env: - name: ConnectionStrings__Default valueFrom: secretKeyRef: name: api key: ConnectionStrings__Default`; deploy/k8s/db.yaml: `- name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD valueFrom: secretKeyRef: name: db key: POSTGRES_PASSWORD`.

argocd-install.sh @ stage-3 only runs `kubectl create namespace argocd`, `kubectl apply -n argocd -f deploy/argocd/install.yaml`, rollout status waits and `kubectl get`/`api-resources`; no Secret, key, plugin or ConfigMap patch is applied.

issues.text: Carried from round 1. The lesson builds three Secrets (db, api, keycloak), but the rebuilt-cluster example only says what happens to db and api. I still cannot tell whether Keycloak's Pod waits too, starts, or is never applied because its wave comes after the database's.
issues.quote: yet the db Pod waits with `CreateContainerConfigError`, the reason a container shows while a Secret it names through `secretKeyRef` does not exist, and the sync never gets past the database's sync wave, so the api is never applied.
issues.fix: Add a short clause saying what happens to Keycloak, e.g. 'and neither is Keycloak' if its wave is after the database's, or say which wave it is in.

issues.text: Carried from round 1. The Core concepts terms are still not bolded, so in later sections I could not tell at a glance which phrases are the defined terms.
issues.quote: - Secret created outside Git — a Secret that a command such as `secrets.sh` sends straight to the API server
issues.fix: Bold the term at the start of each Core concepts item, or mark them another way the house style allows (e.g. italics) so they stand out.

issues.text: New in the changed text. The 'You notice this' sentence now packs four steps (cluster syncs, db Pod waits, what the error means, sync stops at the wave, api never applied) into one sentence. I re-read it twice to see which clause explains the error and which is the consequence.
issues.quote: You notice this when a cluster rebuilt from Git syncs, yet the db Pod waits with `CreateContainerConfigError`, the reason a container shows while a Secret it names through `secretKeyRef` does not exist, and the sync never gets past
issues.fix: Split it into two sentences: end the first after the definition of `CreateContainerConfigError`, then start 'Because that wave never becomes healthy, the sync never reaches the api's wave, so the api is never applied.'
